title: Gene Therapy of Haemophilia: Patient Experiences 2025
summary:
Gene therapy for haemophilia B aims to reduce bleeding. The goal is that, after a single treatment, the body can produce the missing clotting factor (factor IX) on its own, so that regular infusions of this factor may no longer be necessary. To properly assess the benefits of this therapy, it is important not only to look at medical changes, but also to understand how patients personally experienced the treatment and how it affects their long-term well-being.
The aim of this study is therefore to explore patients’ experiences with gene therapy. In addition to medical changes (such as bleeding or the need for medication), physical, emotional, and social aspects will also be examined in order to improve patient care after gene therapy in the future.
Three patients with haemophilia B will be included in the study who received gene therapy approximately 10 years ago as part of the AMT-060 study in Frankfurt or Berlin.
After giving their consent, patients will take part in a one-time telephone interview lasting about 40 to 60 minutes using a question guideline. The conversation will be recorded and written down. In addition basic informations about age, duration of the disease, previous treatment with factor IX and bleeding events will be collected.

interventions.name: Patients who have received factor IX gene therapy will be interviewed by phone.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- patients with haemophilia B
- patients who have participated in a clinical study on factor IX gene therapy in Germany, 
   study centres Frankfurt or Berlin
Exclusion criteria:
- patients who were recruited in other study centres
